literal: Unlearned man's cleverness, exceedingly good even if it is, will not accept, knowledge possessors.
translation: Even if the natural cleverness of an unlearned man is exceedingly good, the wise will not accept it.
modern: படிக்காதவனின் அறிவுக்கூர்மை மிகவும் நன்றாக இருந்தாலும், அறிவுடையவர்கள் அதனை ஏற்றுக்கொள்ள மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that natural cleverness without formal learning is not valued by the wise. The word 'கல்லாதான்' refers to a person who has not acquired learning, while 'ஒட்பம்' denotes natural brilliance or cleverness. Even if such a person's ideas seem exceptionally good ('கழிய நன்று'), those who possess true knowledge ('அறிவுடையார்') will not accept them, because uncultivated intellect lacks depth, discipline, and reliability.
